name: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Small Intestine

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Small Intestine SCC

criteria.description: Histological confirmation of squamous cell carcinoma in small intestine biopsy or resection specimen
Radiological evidence of a mass lesion localized to the small intestine on CT or MRI
Exclusion of primary squamous cell carcinoma from other common sites (e.g., esophagus, lung, skin) to confirm primary small intestine origin
Positive immunohistochemical staining for squamous markers such as p40, p63, and cytokeratin 5/6

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of squamous cell carcinoma in the small intestine with radiological localization and exclusion of other primary sites
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including pathology, radiology, and clinical correlation.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Obstructive small bowel mass causing intermittent intestinal obstruction
Histologically confirmed squamous cell carcinoma in small intestine biopsy
searchTerms: small intestine biopsy showing squamous cancer
cancer cells in small bowel tissue
confirmed squamous cell tumor in intestine

common.symptomName: Persistent abdominal pain localized to mid-abdomen
Nausea and vomiting secondary to partial bowel obstruction
searchTerms: nausea and vomiting from partial bowel blockage
throwing up due to bowel obstruction

common.symptomName: Occult gastrointestinal bleeding leading to iron deficiency anemia

searchTerms: passing dark or red blood in bowel movements

occasional.symptomName: Fatigue related to chronic disease or anemia

rare.symptomName: Jaundice due to biliary obstruction from tumor extension
searchTerms: yellowing skin from bile duct blockage
jaundice due to tumor blocking bile flow
skin and eye yellowing from obstruction
hole in intestine causing severe belly pain

laboratory: Iron deficiency anemia on complete blood count
imaging: CT scan showing localized mass in small intestine with possible bowel obstruction
MRI may demonstrate tumor extent and local invasion
PET scan to exclude metastatic disease and other primary tumors
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; molecular profiling may show TP53 mutations similar to other squamous cell carcinomas
other: Histopathology demonstrating keratinization, intercellular bridges, and squamous differentiation
Immunohistochemistry positive for p40, p63, cytokeratin 5/6

distinguishingFeatures: Glandular histology rather than squamous differentiation
More common than SCC in small intestine
History of primary SCC elsewhere (e.g., lung, esophagus, cervix)
Multiple lesions or widespread disease on imaging
Requires exclusion of primary small intestine origin

redFlags: Weight loss exceeding 10% of body weight over 6 months
references: Orphanet: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Small Intestine - ORPHA:423968
National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) Guidelines for Small Bowel Cancers
